AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: Although the rate of local recurrence (LR) after colorectal cancer surgery has decreased, it still poses major surgical and oncological challenges. The aim of this study, based on an audit from a tertiary referral center, was to evaluate determinants associated with outcomes after surgery for pelvic LR and how these have changed over time.

AbstractText.Label: METHOD
AbstractText.content: Retrospective analysis of all resections for pelvic LR of colorectal cancer performed at the Karolinska University Hospital from January 2003 until August 2009 (period 1) and September 2009 until November 2013 (period 2).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Ninety-five patients with pelvic LR were operated on with a curative intent. An R0-resection was achieved in 77% and an R1-resection in 23%. Lateral compartments were invaded in 48% and this proportion increased in period 2: 37% vs 60% (P = 0.05). R1-resections were associated with a higher risk of local re-recurrence than R0-resections; 64% vs 16% (OR 8.90, 2.71-29.78). Lateral recurrences were associated with a lower R0 resection rate than non-lateral recurrences: 63% vs 90% (OR 5.16, 1.57-19.57), and a higher risk of treatment failure in terms of local re-recurrence or distant metastases or death as first event (HR 1.75, 1.06-2.75). However, in a multivariate analysis only R1-resections remained a significant prognostic factor for treatment failure (HR 2.37, 1.32-4.27).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The proportion of lateral pelvic recurrences has increased overtime. Lateral LR is surgically more difficult to resect and associated with worse prognosis. However, with radical surgery many patients with pelvic locally recurrent colorectal cancer may be offered curative treatment. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
